notes: §1985:VIII.4.9.4 GR1: the file 'must be open in the output, I-O, or extend mode' when WRITE executes; §1985:VIII.1.3.4 gives status 48 for a WRITE 'attempted on a file not open in the I-O, output, or extend mode'. RelativeConnector#Write (reached from KeyedIoEmitter#EmitWrite, edition-invariant) checks the open mode before any record or key rule and answers '48' (FileStatusCode.WriteNotOpenForOutput). Probes at 85: WRITE never-opened, after CLOSE, open INPUT (random, sequential, dynamic) and after a failed OPEN I-O (35) each give 48 and run the USE/INVALID KEY-free path; OUTPUT, random I-O, dynamic OUTPUT and sequential EXTEND give 00; sequential I-O (1985 undefined, the OPEN table forbids it) gives 48 as 2023 defines; OPEN EXTEND on a random file is refused at compile time (COBOL2372, §1985:VIII.4.4.3 SR1). The witness checks OUTPUT, I-O, EXTEND and the 48 into the USE procedure.

next.reason: 1985: the file 'must be open in the output, I-O, or extend mode'; a sequential-access WRITE in I-O mode meets this rule, breaks only the OPEN Table 2, and 1985 status 48 ('not open in the I-O, output, or extend mode') does not cover it: undefined. §2023:14.9.51.4 GR3: 'If the access mode of the write file is sequential, the open mode of the write file connector shall be extend or output', else unsuccessful with '48' (§2023:9.1.13.7 GR8 a); Table 20 of §2023:14.9.27.4 GR8).
